wtp_range.note: Expressed per month for comparability; in practice this audience buys annual/exam-cycle passes, not monthly subscriptions. FX ~INR 88/USD (estimate).

van_westendorp.derivation: too_cheap = 0: every direct competitor gives alerts free (Testbook, Adda247, FreeJobAlert, Sarkari Result sites, Telegram), so there is no quality floor. cheap_but_acceptable = INR 8/mo (INR 99/yr): the 'impulse annual' price point common in Indian edtech promos (PW MTS practice batch INR 399; coupon-site Testbook Pass offers INR 299-349/yr). getting_expensive = modal alert price is INR 0, so anchored instead to ~20% of the nearest paid substitute (Testbook unified Pass ~INR 749/yr = ~INR 62/mo -> INR 12.5/mo) x desire multiplier 1.32 = ~INR 16/mo (~INR 199/yr). too_expensive = capped at the pain threshold: an alerts product cannot cost more than ~2/3 of a full mock-test pass that includes alerts for free -> INR 499/yr = ~INR 41/mo.

desire_premium_rationale: Primary driver = control (1.2-1.5x band); desire_strength_label = 'moderate' so the low end 1.2x is used, not the midpoint. Secondary driver = survival scores 4 (>=3, different from primary) -> +10% bonus => 1.2 x 1.1 = 1.32. Applied to a near-zero base, the premium is almost irrelevant in absolute terms (+INR 4/mo).
recommended_pricing_model: Freemium (ad-supported free tier) + low-priced annual 'exam-season' Pro pass, with a transactional add-on to test: paid application-assist per form. Subscription-only is NOT viable against free alternatives.

pricing_models_considered.fit_rationale: Prep-reminder layer is daily; alert layer is event-driven. Annual pass mirrors Testbook/PW norms.
pricing_models_considered.risk: Core value (alerts) must be free to compete, so the paid tier must sell something else (ad-free, WhatsApp delivery, deeper eligibility, prep plans). India/SEA download-to-paid median ~0.7-1.4% (RevenueCat-cited).

pricing_models_considered.fit_rationale: How every alert aggregator (sarkariresult.com, FreeJobAlert) monetizes.
pricing_models_considered.risk: Head keyword CPC ~$0.01 shows advertisers value this intent near zero; Indian eCPMs are low; requires millions of MAU to matter. Ads also undermine the trust/quiet positioning.

pricing_models_considered.model: Consumables / per-transaction (assisted application, document kit, photo/signature resize + checklist)
pricing_models_considered.fit_rationale: Only non-prep WTP signal found: cyber cafes/CSCs charge INR 30-150 per form (commercial pages; NIOS CSC table ~INR 33).
pricing_models_considered.risk: Operationally heavy; accuracy/liability if a form is rejected; Aadhaar/face-verification flows (mySSC) limit third-party assistance; trust barrier for a new brand.

pricing_models_considered.fit_rationale: RevenueCat global data shows hard paywalls convert ~10.7% vs ~2.1% freemium.
pricing_models_considered.risk: Users will not pay for something Testbook/Adda247/Telegram give free; would kill installs.
Low price ceiling (~INR 49-99); no recurring revenue; Indian Play Store paid-app conversion is poor.

recommended_price.transactional_test: INR 29-49 per assisted application (undercuts cyber cafe INR 30-150)
recommended_price.launch_tactic: Founding-member lifetime at INR 499 (approx 2.5x annual) only as a launch cash/review tactic, capped at first 500 buyers

freemium_conversion_rationale: Category 'utility' typical is 1-4% globally; India/SEA download-to-paid medians are ~0.7-1.4% (RevenueCat via secondary sources) and India revenue per download ~$0.03 (TechCrunch/Sensor Tower). The free tier must contain the core value (alerts), so value gating is weak (the 'pain of free' is just ads). Desire is moderate, not strong. -> 0.8%, at the low end. Flag: unvalidated.

competitive_pricing_range.notes: Alerts: INR 0 everywhere (modal). Max = nearest paid substitute that bundles alerts: Testbook unified Pass ~INR 674-749/yr (~INR 56-62/mo). PW govt batches INR 399-1,999 per batch. Different-model competitor: offline cyber cafe/CSC at INR 30-150 per form (transactional).

category_benchmark_range.india_adjusted_note: Framework benchmarks are US-calibrated. Indian revenue per download is ~1/7 of SEA/LatAm (~$0.03 vs >$0.20). Our target of ~$0.18/mo sits far BELOW the framework's utility minimum ($1/mo) — per the skill's rule this means 'the app may struggle to sustain development'.

b2b2c_potential.rationale: Speculative: coaching institutes, Telegram channel admins, or small edtechs could license a verified, structured notification + eligibility feed/API (INR ~2,000-10,000/mo per institute, estimate, no evidence found). Flag as future expansion only; do not lead with it as a solo indie dev.

market_insights_pricing_signals: monetization_evidence (apps): Testbook unified Pass ~INR 674-749/yr; Testbook FY24 revenue INR 136.7 Cr with INR 84.9 Cr loss
monetization_evidence (apps/web): cyber cafes/CSCs charge INR 30-150 per job application form
web-search: 'sarkari result' CPC ~$0.01 despite 79-124M monthly searches — near-zero commercial value of the alert intent
apps: Adda247 FY25 revenue flat ~INR 217 Cr, loss ~INR 103.6 Cr — even the scaled paid layer is not profitable
pricing_rationale: Monetization evidence exists in the category, but NOT for alerts — it exists for prep (Testbook/PW) and for assisted form filling (cyber cafes). For the idea as stated, effective WTP for alerts is ~INR 0 for most users; a Pro tier at ~INR 199/yr is the realistic target and is UNVALIDATED. The skill's rule applies: when competing with strong free alternatives, the paid tier must deliver something free alternatives structurally can't — here the only candidate with an observed price is 'do the application for me / make me application-ready' (INR 29-49 per form). input user_extraction.json does not exist, so pain intensity was inferred from market evidence; proceeded without it.
